test_title: PYST 45: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 24 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which option correctly explains the fundamental difference between input and output devices in a computer system?

options.text: Input devices enable users to send data into the system, while output devices communicate processed information back to the user.
Input devices run pre-loaded instructions from memory, whereas output devices collect environmental data.
Input devices change user inputs into digital format, while output devices permanently save system data.
Input devices directly interact with the CPU, while output devices work independently without CPU involvement.

solution:
The correct answer is option 1","

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Input devices** are hardware components used to send raw data or user commands into a computer system for processing. Examples include keyboards, mice, and microphones.
 
• **Output devices** are hardware components that display, project, or otherwise communicate the processed information from the computer to the user. Examples include monitors, printers, and speakers.
 
• Input devices serve as a bridge to collect data from the user or environment, while output devices deliver the results of data processing back to the user.
 
• Keyboards and scanners are input devices that convert analog or physical user input into digital signals, whereas output devices like monitors display digital information in a human-readable format.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **Input Devices:**

 
 
• Examples: Keyboard, mouse, scanner, joystick, microphone.
 
• Purpose: Collect raw data or commands from the user and send them to the CPU for processing.
 
• They often use interfaces like USB, Bluetooth, or wireless connections to connect to the system.
 
 
 
• **Output Devices:**
 
 
• Examples: Monitor, printer, speakers, projectors, headphones.
 
• Purpose: Convert processed digital data into a human-perceivable form, such as images, sound, or text.
 
• Output devices often rely on graphic processing units (GPUs) or audio processors for rendering data.
 
 
 
• **Input/Output (I/O) Devices:**
 
 
• Some devices, like touchscreens, function as both input and output devices.
 
• These devices can display information (output) and allow user interaction (input) simultaneously.
 
 
 
• **Communication Between Devices:**
 
 
• Input devices send signals to the CPU for processing, while output devices receive processed data from the CPU.
 
• The entire process is managed through buses, drivers, and system software.
